assessment: The incumbent supplies removable partitions in an assembled, configurable product, but recorded median workshop time exceeds eight minutes and only seven of ten observed customers arranged it unaided. Five missing/incorrect-part reports flag a contents risk without establishing five verified omissions. A limiting observation is D2-O6: repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, so slow completion is not universal. Mixed batches contained the longest orders, but layout complexity and switching remain confounded. D2-O5 likewise does not support width alone as the insertion explanation. These synthetic observations establish neither causes nor pilot success.

openings.claim: Selecting and checking parts across changing orders may contribute to excess time and contents errors; reusable, order-specific staging guides may reduce both.
openings.delta: Stage one complete order against a component checklist before insertion, instead of selecting directly from shared shape bins throughout assembly.
openings.prediction: For matched layout and color, guides reduce selection/checking time and independently audited contents errors; an effect confined to six-compartment insertion would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Have both workers repeat matched orders with and without guides in counterbalanced mixed and grouped sequences. Reuse available samples; time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately and audit contents against orders. Include guide preparation in workshop time accounting.
assumptions: Guides leave product geometry, capacity, colors and compartment counts unchanged.
Preparation and trials fit the delivery schedule and verified initial and recurring cost caps.

openings.claim: Ambiguity in identifying the short partition location may limit unaided arrangement even when all correct parts are present.
openings.delta: Replace the three-layout diagram with a diagram of the ordered layout that identifies the short partition and its orientation.
openings.prediction: With independently verified complete kits, the specific diagram reduces placement questions and increases unaided completion relative to the existing diagram.
openings.probe: Allocate the ten participants across matched first-use sessions with either diagram; record unaided completion, placement errors and questions. Treat this as a directional probe, then assess the stated completeness, time and customer targets in the 60-unit pilot.
assumptions: Diagram production stays within both cost caps and the fixed delivery date.
Supplied parts and removable joints remain unchanged.
